text:
maria: Heads-up — dashboard tail numbers look off for /v1/generate after the quota/routing tweak this morning. p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~950ms but backend logs show no throughput spike.
jake: I noticed that too. The rollout note mentioned 'prefer-low-latency' but didn't call out sample attribution. Any routing weight changes?
alex: deploy-bot indicates policy change at 1761000900: `policy:update prefer-low-latency -> weight 0.6` :deploy-bot:
deploy-bot: policy:update completed by @ops at 2025-06-12T15:55:00Z
sophia: Quick clarity check — how are percentiles computed in console? Are we merging per-route tdigest shards or recomputing from raw rows across routes? That could explain the p99 delta when traffic shifts.
maria: Console uses tdigest rollups from ingestion and merges them by endpoint. We don't recompute from raw rows for the default view, so changes in route weights can shift which tdigest dominates the merged digest.
jake: Did a tiny local repro: ran per-route p99 and global p99 over raw rows. Per-route p99s were routeA=450ms, routeB=1800ms; global raw-row p99 was 520ms but console shows ~950ms. So merged tdigest seems to behave differently than raw aggregation.
alex: Can you paste the exact repro queries? I'll compare with the merge code.
sophia: Repro steps I used:
```
-- per-route
SELECT route_tag, percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99
FROM sample_traces
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate'
GROUP BY route_tag;
-- global
SELECT percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99
FROM sample_traces
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate';
```
Observed: per-route p99s = [routeA: 450, routeB: 1800], global raw p99 = 520, console-merged p99 ~= 950.
maria: That matches an explanation where routeB's tdigest was sparse and the merged digest exaggerated tail because of bucketization differences.
jake: Sounds like routing weight increased relative impact of routeB's digest. Since tdigest merge is not identical to raw-sample percentile, the p99 can shift nonlinearly when proportions change.
sophia: Short-term UX/ops mitigations proposed:
- show per-route p50/p95/p99 alongside the merged percentile in the latency pane
- add a "percentile provenance" indicator that, on hover, explains aggregation method (tdigest merge vs raw-row calc) and sample counts
- surface raw sample counts per route in a debug view + a quick "recompute exact p99 from raw rows" link for audits
alex: From backend side, we can also emit a warning flag when the merged tdigest percentile differs from a sampled raw-row percentile by >15% so the dashboard surfaces a caution icon.
maria: Action items:
- @jake open PR to update UI: surface per-route percentiles, add tooltip copy, include unit tests comparing digest merge vs raw percentile on synthetic data
- @alex add an internal endpoint to expose per-route raw counts and provide the exact SQL snippet to recompute global percentile
- @sophia draft a short alert rule and doc blurb for support/CSM explaining when to distrust merged p99
- I'll write a brief note to support explaining the change after deploy
jake: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/4821 — includes screenshots and a test harness. Please review.
alex: Reviewing now. We'll gate the UI behind a feature flag so we can roll slowly.
sophia: Small UX nit: avoid the word 'tdigest' in the consumer-facing tooltip; use 'sampled merge' and 'may differ from exact raw-sample percentile' instead.
maria: Agreed. Also schedule a quick postmortem blurb after deploy so CSM has a clear explanation for customers who ask about p99 changes. Thanks all.
